citation.title: Exploring the Influence of Artificial Intelligence Usage on Ethical Decision Making Among Public Sector Employees: Insights into Moral Identity and Service Motivation

reading.source_scope_note: Cross-sectional self-report survey of 417 Chinese public-sector employees recruited through managers’ WeChat networks by convenience and snowball methods. SEM, bootstrap mediation and regression moderation analyze the same data. The AI-usage items primarily concern expected benefits, attitudes and intentions; ethical-behavior items are stated intentions. No randomized AI adoption, observed ethical conduct or identified causal mediation.
access_limits: All18 supplied pages read. DOI web-reader access returned403,but the public journal PDF was accessible through its published endpoint and checksum-matched. No credential or challenge bypass.

Raw data are available only on reasonable request to an author. No author contact was authorized or attempted;no responses,SEM syntax,bootstrap draws,exact covariance matrix,organization identifiers or final item map were obtained.

The full English questionnaire appendix was read. A Chinese translation/back-translation process is described,but the actual administered Chinese instrument was not supplied. No additional dataset or supplement was identified.

Primary Wiley abstract/Crossref metadata for Park/Woo/Kim2024 were checked:the original AAAW instrument has25 items and six attitude dimensions. Full original,all supplementary appendices and raw validation data were not read. Current eight-item adaptation is not the original25-item validated scale.

Wang/VanWitteloostuijn/Heine2020 primary abstract,introduction/definition and conclusion passages were read for the public-service-motivation construct and its plural motives. Not the full original theory article or underlying studies;no extra full-review or independent behavior-paper credit.

Louangrath2017 is identified in this article’s bibliography as a sample-size paper. The intended AlHalbusi2021,Wright2013/2016,Weichun2011 and Vandenabeele2007 full source identities are incomplete/missing here and were not guessed. Other cited books/articles were not independently fully read.

Consent is labeled Not applicable despite a human survey,and explicit institutional approval is not stated. Cover-letter/privacy language is described;this does not prove missing consent or misconduct. Retain the documentation discrepancy without identifying/profiling respondents.
No real public-sector deployment,individual political/mental-state assessment,author-code execution,paid inference or full-paper Markdown archive.

study.sample: 500distributed,432returned,417retained after15 invalid responses. Return rate86.4%;usable-response rate83.4%. Demographic tables each sum417:211female206male;108aged21–30,16231–40,13041–50,1751–60. Province/organization sampling probabilities,network dependence and response exclusions are not fully documented;convenience/snowball recruitment does not establish population representativeness.
study.design: March–June2024 online Questionnaire Star survey. All major variables are contemporaneous self-reports. The authors explicitly acknowledge common-method/social-desirability concerns and inability to establish causality in their limitations;preserve this rather than claim complete ignorance of the problem.
study.ai_measure: Eight appendix items describe confidence,control,performance,accomplishment,independence,enjoyment and future intention. Most say would,intend or future. This is largely attitude/expected utility/intention content,not a behavioral measure of frequency,duration,task exposure or actual AI use.
study.service_motivation: Five appendix PSM items include meaningful public service,community impact,society over personal achievement and effort for society. PSM5 instead asks openness to adopting AI for efficiency. That item overlaps the purported predictor,so a positive association may partly reflect shared AI-acceptance content. It should not enter the canonical definition of public-service motivation.
study.moral_identity: The introduction sometimes describes moral cognition/knowledge as identity,but the methods/appendix correctly emphasize the importance of ethical values to self-concept. Keep the established identity definition rather than merge identity,knowledge,awareness and moral reasoning into one construct.
study.norms_and_outcome: Four moral-norm items combine duty,public good,morally sound decisions and self-evaluation. Eight ethical-behavior statements are future-tense intentions,including accountability,resource use,gifts,confidentiality and honest reporting. They do not measure actual corruption,observed decisions or a verified improvement in ethics.
study.culture_and_items: Methods say10 culture items,appendix lists5,and culture is absent from the loading/AVE/discriminant tables. UA/EEB begin with8items,pretest saysUA5/EEB5 removed,and Table2 shows7renumbered labels each. Without a mapping,one cannot identify which original item was retained/dropped or assert a dropped item was definitely analyzed.
study.reliability: Reported standardized loadings reproduce CR/AVE within rounding for all five displayed factors. AVEs approximateUA.511,ESM.664,MN.681,MID.520,EEB.502;CRs.880,.908,.895,.844,.876. Alpha and CR matching for several factors is not proof of fabrication. These checks do not establish construct validity or actual behavior.
study.discriminant_validity: Table3 off-diagonal correlations range.307–.516,contradicting prose saying all exceed.494. Diagonal square-root AVEs and the displayed Fornell–Larcker inequalities are coherent. The matrix does not supply HTMT values despite the heading. Overall CFA/SEM fit indices,residuals and measurement alternatives are not fully reported.
study.common_method: Harman first factor30.1% below50% is used to downplay CMV. A single-factor threshold cannot establish the absence of shared-method bias,criterion overlap or social-desirability distortion. No independent-source,temporal or experimental validation is supplied.
study.paths: Reported pathsUA→ESM.342,UA→MN.392,UA→MID.488;ESM→EEB.271,MN→EEB.190,MID→EEB.310. Preserve them as reported same-sample associations under uncertain scaling/controls,not identified causal effects. Figure1 shows3controls,methods names4,and output does not fully document their treatment.
study.mediation: Table5 gives total.423,direct.097(with unlabeled.106),specific indirects.085,.069,.140. Direct plus the three indirects is.391,leaving.032if these are one model/metric. Products of displayed Table4 paths also differ. Scaling,separate model fits or unreported paths could explain differences;do not invent corrected coefficients or call the causal mediation complete.
study.moderation: Table6 interaction terms areESM−.293,MN−.329,MID−.073(NS). Under stated higher-is-supportiveOC coding,the first two imply weaker AI slopes at higher culture scores. Figure4 matches attenuation,but Figure3 labels highOC as the steeper positive service-motivation line,the opposite sign. Which legend/coefficient is wrong cannot be resolved without original output/data.
study.moderated_mediation: Table7 negative indicesESM−.057,CI[−.097,−.025],MN−.044,CI[−.080,−.015];MID−.018,CI[−.049,.010]. The first two CIs exclude zero,the third does not. The prose erroneously calls the third significant while rejectingH8c. High-culture point estimates near/below zero do not establish a genuine harmful reversal.
study.regression_reporting: Conditional calculations fromN417 and roundedR² suggest someStep2 F entries resemble change F while another resembles overall F. Rounding and unreported controls/model choices preclude exact reconstruction. Keep this as a labeling/output question,not a proof that every regression calculation is impossible.
study.inference: SEM arrows and bootstrap nonzero indirect intervals do not establish temporal order,causal mediation or a benefit of adopting AI. Reverse causation,shared positive self-image,common content,unmeasured confounding and organizational/network clustering remain plausible. Recommendations to increase AI use for ethical improvement require prospective evidence.

summary: Add Public service motivation as a distinct public-interest motivation construct,without building AI adoption into its definition. Enrich the existing moral-identity entry and add non-counted context for adoption intention,performance expectations and norm internalization. Preserve reproducible measurement arithmetic while documenting misnamed variables,source-provenance gaps,mediation accounting and the local figure-sign mismatch.

findings.definition: Motivation to serve the public interest and contribute to the well-being of society.

evidence.quote: Meaningful public service is very important to me

findings.novelty_rationale: A named public-administration/work-motivation construct absent from current names/aliases. It concerns a public-interest orientation,not merely moral identity,the intrinsic enjoyment of an activity,a desire to leave a legacy,public-sector employment or willingness to adopt AI. Public-service goals may involve several motives and need not imply complete absence of self-interest.
findings.evidence_scope: Directly discussed and measured through a five-item adaptation in the read survey. Four appendix items express public-service or societal concern; the fifth overlaps AI acceptance. Reported mediation is not causally identified, and numerical and provenance problems remain. Targeted Wang et al. (2020) theory passages support the broader construct, not the current AI-effect claims.
findings.boundary: A stated public-interest motive does not prove ethical conduct, unselfishness, competence or legitimate public authority. Different conceptions of the public good can conflict; rights and affected people still matter. The construct can apply beyond government employees. AI acceptance is not part of its definition, and model service language does not establish a felt human motive.
findings.ai_proposal: In an authorized public-service task, specify the relevant public-interest goals, rights, affected groups and service criteria. Test whether an assistant preserves those criteria when convenience, image or performance targets pull in another direction. Compare its actual choices with stated commitments; do not infer public benefit from an institutional label or from increased AI adoption.
findings.origin: Public administration / organizational psychology / public-interest motivation
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human motivation construct discussed in a fully read self-report survey; causal effects of AI usage and a model’s subjective public-service motive are not established.

terminology_sources.title: A Moral Theory of Public Service Motivation
terminology_sources.consulted: Targeted primary abstract, introduction, definition and conclusion passages only. Describes public-interest and societal welfare orientation, plural motives and extension beyond public employment. Full theory article and its underlying studies not read; no independent full-paper or experiment credit.

findings.definition: The importance of moral qualities to a person’s self-concept.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while separating motivation,self-concept,attitudes,intentions and observed conduct. A local scale label or composite component is not a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Five self-report items concern ethical self-concept and commitment. The reported same-sample association with an ethical-intention composite does not establish a new causal effect of AI use.
findings.boundary: Identity differs from moral knowledge/awareness and actual conduct. Preserve the canonical self-concept definition despite inconsistent prose labels. Self-presentation,overlapping values and common-method effects remain possible;no validated machine moral self is demonstrated.

findings.definition: Plans or stated likelihood of incorporating AI technology into future activities.

evidence.quote: I intend to continue using AI

findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while separating motivation,self-concept,attitudes,intentions and observed conduct. A local scale label or composite component is not a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: At least two items inside the variable labeled AI usage are future-intention statements;PSM5 also asks openness to using AI.
findings.boundary: Context only:the composite is not a separately validated intention factor or observed use. Do not reinterpret positive paths as actual adoption causing ethical improvement,or treat an intention as authorization.

findings.definition: Believing that using a tool will improve one’s task effectiveness or productivity.

evidence.quote: Utilizing AI would improve my job performance

findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while separating motivation,self-concept,attitudes,intentions and observed conduct. A local scale label or composite component is not a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Expected job-performance benefits are included among the AI-usage items.
findings.boundary: Context only:an anticipated benefit is not measured productivity or a distinct identified expectancy effect. The current mixed composite combines utility,control,enjoyment and intention rather than isolating a single construct.

findings.definition: Adopting a norm as an internal evaluative standard that guides judgment and conduct beyond immediate external prompts or sanctions.

evidence.quote: Following ethics when using AI is both my responsibility and duty

findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while separating motivation,self-concept,attitudes,intentions and observed conduct. A local scale label or composite component is not a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Moral-norm items state duty,public benefit and a positive moral self-evaluation.
findings.boundary: Context only:declared endorsement and future intentions do not demonstrate internalization beyond prompts/sanctions or observed justified conduct. Institutional norms need not all be ethical,and the survey supplies no behavioral generalization test.

aggregate_checks.scope: Printed aggregate arithmetic only. Standardized-loading formulas and regression-distribution checks are conditional;no raw questionnaire responses,bootstrap samples,SEM syntax or original regression output were obtained.

table3.finding: Printed off-diagonal values range.307–.516,not all above.494. Diagonal square roots of reported AVEs and the displayed Fornell–Larcker comparison are coherent;HTMT is not recovered from this matrix.

mediation_accounting.limit: Different scaling,models or unreported paths may explain a mismatch. No corrected effect value or causally complete mediation is inferred.

ESM.limit: Rounded R² can shift these values. F labels may mix overall-model and change statistics;unreported controls/models could also differ. Do not invent exact original output.

MN.limit: Rounded R² can shift these values. F labels may mix overall-model and change statistics;unreported controls/models could also differ. Do not invent exact original output.

MID.limit: Rounded R² can shift these values. F labels may mix overall-model and change statistics;unreported controls/models could also differ. Do not invent exact original output.

moderation.finding: Under displayed positive OC coding,both slopes decrease with OC. Figure3 legend instead displays a larger AI slope for high OC;Figure4 displays attenuation. Neither the correct legend nor corrected coefficient can be recovered.

aggregate_checks.p_limit: These are normal-reference checks from printed index/SE ratios,not recovered bootstrap p-values. p<.000 is impossible notation;95% bootstrap intervals support their stated inclusion/exclusion of zero but do not justify every displayed significance star.

source_corrections.correction: Describe this as the article’s AI-related attitude/expected-benefit/intention composite,not verified frequency or intensity of actual AI use. Appendix wording would,intend andfuture directly supports this distinction. No new questionnaire score is computed without raw data/item mapping.

The original paper is an attitudes-at-work scale,25items across6dimensions,Journal of Occupational and Organizational Psychology97(3):920–951. Current8items are an adaptation,not the unchanged original validated scale;document item selection and validity. The original full paper was not read in this pass.

Methods attribute the8-item scale to Louangrath2017,whose listed work is Minimum sample size method based on survey scales. Appendix instead attributes it to AlHalbusi2021,missing from the bibliography. Clarify the intended original and adaptation;do not present the sample-size article as verified provenance of an ethical-behavior instrument or invent the missing citation.

Off-diagonal correlations range.307–.516;they are not all above.494. The diagonal root-AVE values and displayed Fornell–Larcker inequalities do reconcile. This correction does not manufacture HTMT results or prove overall construct validity.
432/500=86.4%return rate;417/500=83.4%usable-response rate. The printed83.4%is arithmetically correct for usable cases,but its return-rate label is imprecise.

The displayed95%CI[−.049,.010] includes zero,and the hypothesis is rejected in the text/table. Replace the local word significant with not significant at the95%criterion. Do not claim the authors supportedH8c throughout.
The moral-norms→ethical-behavior path.190corresponds toH5,as Table4 correctly labels it. The preceding service-motivation path isH4.

A probability cannot be below zero. Use a valid reporting threshold verified from original output;roundedp=.000is not exact zero. Do not automatically replace every Table7 index label withp<.001:normal-reference checks from printed index/SE values do not support that blanket threshold,and exact bootstrap p-values are unavailable.

Wright2013/2016,Weichun2011,AlHalbusi2021 and Vandenabeele2007 lack complete matching entries in the inspected65-item bibliography. Full identities are needed before treating their instruments or claims as independently verified. No guessed author expansion,DOI or full-original reading is supplied.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Rendered Figure3 labels highOC as the stronger positive AI/service-motivation slope,while Table6 interaction−.293 and Table7 negative moderated-mediation index imply attenuation under stated coding. Figure4 fits the negative moral-norm interaction. A local legend,sign or model mismatch needs original output;do not swap every legend or invent corrected data.

Total.423 does not equal direct.097 plus.085+.069+.140=.391 if all values share a model/metric. Unlabeled(.106),different standardizations/separate model fits or omitted paths could matter. The current report does not resolve them. No replacement effect is inferred and non-significant direct effects do not prove complete causal mediation.

WithN417 and displayed2/3predictor models,ESM/MN Step2F values resemble incremental F rather than overall F,whereasMID Step2 resembles overall F. Rounding and unspecified controls prevent exact recovery. Label overall/change statistics and disclose full model output rather than call all values arithmetically impossible.

Methods’ UA5/EEB5 deletion,7relabeled loading items,8-item appendix lists and10-versus5culture items need an administration-to-analysis map. Labels may have been renumbered;one cannot prove discarded originals were actually used from matching codes alone.

The reported matrix is Pearson/Fornell–Larcker style,not the missing HTMT matrix. Culture loadings/AVE/discriminant information and standard overall CFA/SEM fit details are not supplied. A high alpha or first-factor threshold does not resolve these construct-validity questions.

Human survey data coexist with an Informed Consent Not applicable statement. Cover-letter and confidentiality descriptions do not resolve the discrepancy,and no institutional approval statement was found. Ask for documentation in a scholarly review;do not infer coercion,fabrication or identify respondents. This assistant did not contact the authors.

Labels vary across abstract,introduction,results and conclusions. Appendix self-concept items fit identity rather than a knowledge test. Preserve the established ontology definition and do not treat all three labels as exact synonyms.

methodological_limits: Cross-sectional same-source data identify no temporal or causal benefit of AI adoption and no causal mediation. SEM arrows and bootstrap intervals cannot establish that order by themselves.

The predictor is largely attitude/expectancy/intention,the outcome largely ethical intention,andPSM5 shares AI-acceptance content. Construct labels must follow item content rather than substitute actual use and observed virtue.

Convenience/snowball sampling via manager networks does not establish a representative sample or independent observations. Institutional climate is measured through individuals;organization counts,nesting and clustering treatment are not documented.
A Harman first-factor result under50%does not rule out method bias,content overlap or social desirability. Alpha,CR/AVE and Fornell–Larcker comparisons do not establish behavioral or causal validity.

Mediation point accounting and graph/sign inconsistencies reduce confidence in precise mechanism claims. Different metrics,model fits or F conventions can explain some discrepancies,so original output is needed before assigning corrected values.

Full mediation is not proven by a non-significant direct estimate. High-culture near-zero negative point estimates and null moral-identity moderation do not establish equivalence,absence or harmful reversal.
Conditional normal-reference p checks are not recovered bootstrap p-values. Preserve what95%CIs show without interpreting invalidp<.000notation literally or inventing exact significance.

The authors acknowledge cross-sectional,CMV and social-desirability limitations. Their stronger practical recommendations still require prospective evidence,but that is different from alleging they omitted every limitation.

Source instruments require complete citations and adaptation maps. Do not count a sample-size reference as a validated ethical-behavior scale or a25-item attitude instrument as an unchanged8-item usage scale.
Human public-service motivation,self-concept and stated ethics do not establish an AI’s subjective motives,actual moral agency,legal authority or a universal right to expand task scope.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: All reliability values are numerically impossible
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The rounded standardized loadings reproduce CR/AVE values within rounding for all five displayed factors. Matching alpha/CR values do not independently prove fabrication.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Demographic or usable-response totals do not add up
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Every demographic dimension sums417,and432−15=417. The problem is the return-versus-usable label,not a failed headcount.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Figure3 and Figure4 both support the same interaction sign
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Actual rendered legends differ:Figure3 depicts positive slope moderation,Figure4 attenuation. Inspect figures rather than infer identical direction from their titles.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The charts imply impossible scores in the thousands
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Comma labels are decimal formatting,e.g.5,000means5.000 in the plotted1–5context. They are not evidence of5000-point Likert scores.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Table6 mixed F values prove every regression is wrong
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Some values are compatible with incremental rather than overall F,and rounded R² changes need not equal differences of displayed values exactly. Unreported model details remain unresolved.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: UA5/EEB5 appearing proves no item was removed
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Renumbered7-item tables can coexist with removal from an8-item original. A codebook is needed before deciding which original question each final code represents.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The authors never acknowledge causality or method bias
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The conclusion explicitly acknowledges self-report/social-desirability bias and cross-sectional limits and recommends longitudinal/experimental work.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: A new definition requires accepting every reported causal claim
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Public service motivation is distinguishable from the uncertain AI-adoption pathway. Preserve its verified meaning and openly qualify this study’s measurement/inference problems.

cross_paper_learning.finding: A term named behavior may actually be an intention or post-exposure report. Use item wording and response order before interpreting an effect,and preserve both successful arithmetic checks and genuine discrepancies.
AI adoption intention is distinct from adoption and patient/public outcomes. A positive attitude or intervention response does not by itself authorize deployment or prove ethical benefit.
Moral identity is ethical self-concept,not a diagnostic label or a guarantee of moral conduct. Preserve definition boundaries when a paper inconsistently relabels constructs.

Visual verification prevents false table/graph criticisms. Figure3’s actual legend contradicts the negative coefficient,while Figure4 does not;do not generalize a local discrepancy without inspecting both.

deferred.term: Organizational culture as a new behavior
deferred.reason: An institutional/contextual umbrella and mixed scale here,with incomplete item/validity reporting. Do not add a broad duplicate category or a new principle from this moderator label.

deferred.term: Moral cognition/identity/perception as synonymous new rows
deferred.reason: Different constructs are inconsistently named;actual appendix content supports the existing moral-identity entry. No new independent mechanisms are established.
Cross-sectional mixed self-report measures and reporting inconsistencies do not establish the claimed causal mechanism.

deferred.term: New norm-compliance or public-sector virtue effect
deferred.reason: Future intentions and scale endorsement are not observed conduct or proof of justified ethics. Preserve specific existing boundaries instead of a generic new virtue row.

limitations: One public-interest motivation construct added;one existing concept directly enriched and three receive non-counted measurement context. Catalogue becomes817 across the same eleven categories. Printed-aggregate checks are retained without raw-data replication claims. No extra principle,page,automatic harm edge,forced paper quota,invented annual total or full-paper Markdown archive.
